title: The import Statement
subtopics: Name conflicts and fully qualified names
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of the import statement and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—importing classes and interfaces—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study the import statement with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you organize code and control access through packages, modules, and deliberate dependencies. In this lesson, focus on importing classes and interfaces and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Primitive variables store values of the eight primitive types. Choose a type that represents the domain and range required; use exact decimal arithmetic for monetary values when appropriate. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect importing classes and interfaces with wildcard imports before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Importing classes and interfaces
items.text: Primitive variables store values of the eight primitive types. Choose a type that represents the domain and range required; use exact decimal arithmetic for monetary values when appropriate.

items.title: Wildcard imports
items.text: Packages organize names and access boundaries; the module system adds explicit module dependencies and exports. Keep public API surface intentional and verify classpath/module-path settings when troubleshooting.

items.title: Static imports
items.text: Packages organize names and access boundaries; the module system adds explicit module dependencies and exports. Keep public API surface intentional and verify classpath/module-path settings when troubleshooting.

items.title: Name conflicts and fully qualified names
items.text: Packages organize names and package-level access; the module system adds declared dependencies and exports. Diagnose classpath and module-path errors separately from ordinary source-code errors. Apply that reasoning specifically to name conflicts and fully qualified names and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Keep package declarations aligned with source folders and import only the APIs used. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: build the smallest program that demonstrates importing classes and interfaces. Change one input, predict the result, and add one boundary or invalid case before considering the task complete.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
